newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-YOUNG ALLOWS NZ TO DECLARE ON HUGE SCORE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-YOUNG ALLOWS NZ TO DECLARE ON HUGE SCORE.

text.p: New Zealand was able to declare at the huge total of 586 for seven at tea on the second day of the first test against Sri Lanka on Saturday thanks to a brilliant undefeated double century by Bryan Young.
Young's score of 267 was the second highest in tests for New Zealand, only behind Martin Crowe's 299 also scored against Sri Lanka, in 1990/91.
Young scored 148 of his runs in boundaries, most of them through the offside and many of them from his trademark offdrive from the back foot.
The New Zealand total was the second highest in this country's test history behind the 671 for four scored against Sri Lanka in Wellington six years ago when Crowe scored his 299.
New Zealand scored their runs at around four runs an over, with most of the batsmen contributing.
Young and Chris Cairns, 70, shared a sixth wicket stand of 123 in 141 minutes.
Four of the six bowlers used by Sri Lanka conceded more than 100 runs. Left arm seamer Chaminda Vaas was the most impressive of the tourists, taking four for 144 off 35 overs.
